newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to toughen checks on foreign vessels.
newsitem.headline: Japan to toughen checks on foreign vessels.

text.p: Japan said on Tuesday it would toughen checks on foreign vessels stopping at its ports because of an increase in disasters at sea.
Although the announcement follows Japan's worst-ever oil spill, Ministry of Transport officials said the decision to beef up the inspections was made last year.
Japan currently has about 400 auditors who check both Japanese and foreign vessels, a ministry official said.
Starting from April, the number will be increased by up to 10 percent, with 50 of them stationed at 14 ports and inspecting only foreign vessels.
The announcement follows an oil spill from an ageing Russian tanker carrying 19,000 (133,000 barrels) tonnes of heavy fuel oil.

The 13,157-tonne Nakhodka, a 26-year-old vessel taking a load of heavy fuel oil from China to Russia, broke in two during stormy weather in early January, spilling much of its cargo and polluting rich fishing grounds and tourist beaches on the Sea of Japan coast.
Officials are calling it Japan's worst spill ever.
The ministry official said it would not be possible to check all foreign vessels making port calls in Japan, but the inspections would be more thorough.
"We may take further measures to toughen checks due to the oil spill from the Russian tanker," the official said.

The recent growth in "flags of convenience" -- shipping firms registering their vessels with countries such as Liberia and Panama for economic reasons -- has led to an increase in the number of ageing ships with inexperienced crews, shipping industry sources said.
Tougher tax and accounting systems, higher labour and maintenance costs and various legal restrictions have prompted a decline in Japanese-flagged ships.
As of July 1 last year, Japanese freighters and tankers over 2,000 gross registered tons totalled 191, down 27 from a year earlier, according to the ministry.
The peak in Japanese-flagged ships was 1,580 vessels in 1972, the ministry said.
